note: All tunable numbers in one place (GAME EXPANSION; Bob's spec: balance lives in data files).

calendar._note: B8-029 (owner-approved 2026-10-19): one calendar on the world clock. A year is year_days game days (12 real minutes each at game_minutes_per_second 2.0); the seasons follow in order, season_days long each (the last takes any remainder). Ages are in these years.

life._note: B8-029 human life (numbers are provisional, docs/BUILD_DECISIONS.md). Stages by age in years. Natural death: from mortality_from a villager has a daily chance rising as mortality_yearly_max * ((age - from) / (certain_at - from)) ^ mortality_curve, mortality_yearly_max being a hazard per calendar year converted to the day by Life.per_year_to_per_day (TIME-02), and dies for certain at certain_at. Partnering and births are explicit relationships (NPC.partner, mother, father, children), never inferred from a shared house.

relations._note: CRT-01..07 (owner 2026-10-19; numbers are agent proposals, provisional). A gift adds gift_regard (half for a merely useful thing) and, between people who may court, gift_attraction by kind; a favourite (Relations.favourites: the receiver's trade, or food when hungry and medicine when hurt) counts favourite_factor times, a gift repeated from the last three repeat_factor; a second gift in a day counts nothing. Help adds help_regard. befriend_at regard lets the player befriend (no proposal). court_at attraction (and court_min_days days known) lets one ask to court; a proposal is accepted after propose_min_days of courting at propose_at with marry_min_days days known, else declined with too_soon_penalty attraction lost. Ties cool by decay_per_day (attraction; half for regard) on days without contact. Villagers take an interest at npc_court_chance a day in someone they have come to know and each dawn give a gift they hold; time together counts as it happens (shared, seek). Friends trade at friend_price better and back the player before a guard.
relations._chemistry_note: How well a pair clicks: chemistry_min + chemistry_span * u^2 (u fixed per pair and world): most pairs little, a few a great deal. Time together builds attraction times chemistry; gifts do not depend on it.
relations._refuse_note: CRT-12: a proposal is refused when the one asked does not mean to marry (unwilling_percent of people, fixed per person), when the suitor is a known killer (any villager slain) or notorious (notoriety_refuse crimes seen in notoriety_days; each killing counts killing_weight), when their regard is below marry_regard, or when someone else courting them holds more of their heart. Harm reaches those close to the one harmed: kin_harm_share to their family, friend_harm_share to their friends; killing a villager is kill_harm.
relations._seek_note: CRT-11: an unpartnered adult with seek.coins or a gift in hand spends seek.chance of evenings beside the one they court (or their closest friend), first buying a gift with seek.gift_coins to spare; without the means, seek.poor_chance of evenings and no gift.
relations._close_note: CRT-10 (owner: closeness over time weighs most; no marrying in ten minutes of button presses). The player's minutes within close.tiles of a villager (same place, awake) are sampled every sample_minutes; the nearest one, whose name is up to talk to, counts focus_factor; regard_per_hour and attraction_per_hour, at most daily_regard a day from closeness; known_minutes near in a day make it a day known. Every channel adds within regard_daily_cap and attraction_daily_cap a day. Stages need separate days known: court_min_days to court, marry_min_days (and propose_min_days of courting) to marry. Killing a bandit or a wolf or bear near villagers: defend_regard (once a day each). A crime seen: witness_harm; suffered: victim_harm.
relations._shared_note: CRT-08/09 (owner: shared experiences start relationships; proximity about 1 point, a conversation 0.25, later ones about 0.11). Each hour, people awake within near_tiles share it once (an hour together is the unit): work (both working at the same trade or workplace) work_regard, evening company social_regard, otherwise met_regard; *_attraction between people who may court; at most daily_cap regard a pair a day from shared hours (attraction in proportion). A conversation with the player also counts that hour as shared, then adds talk_first the first time a day and talk_more the next, each later one talk_decay times the one before (attraction talk_attraction_share of it). Time together while courting builds attraction courting_factor times as fast. Villagers never again take an interest in someone who refused them for good, and take an interest only in someone known on interest_days days with interest_at attraction or more.

_overworld_note: Chunks (32 x 32 tiles) of the overworld drawn beyond the camera's chunk; chunks more than one beyond are freed. 2 covers a zoomed-out phone view with room to spare. Agent proposal for B8-011.
_child_food_note: A child gets hungry this much as fast as an adult, so eats this share of an adult's food; every household and village food reckoning weights children the same way (NPCBrain.food_factor). NPCs have no ages yet, so the role decides. Agent proposal, provisional: balance review pending (docs/BUILD_DECISIONS.md).
_sprint_note: B8-027: sprint multiplies the player's speed by sprint_speed and costs sprint_stamina_per_sec net of regeneration; it ends when stamina runs out and cannot start below sprint_min_stamina. LT (the left trigger) toggles it on a pad (owner correction, B8-027; L3 is unbound); Shift is held on a keyboard unless sprint_toggle is true (then Shift toggles). Agent proposal, provisional.

local_supply._note: B14 (owner: pricing by availability for sale within a certain diameter): a seller's asking price falls by weight x the units of the item that other traders (jobs, and anyone keeping a counter) and the player's open stall and shops offer within radius tiles, counting at most cap units; a lone seller asks the full scarcity price. What buyers offer is unchanged. Agent proposal, provisional.

tree_growth._note: PROVISIONAL (agent proposal, owner approval pending): the tree lifecycle (Trees, tools/living_forest.py art). A felled mature tree is a stump for tree_regrow_seasons, then a sapling that grows sapling -> young -> growing -> mature; the stage lengths are in calendar seasons (TIME-02: read through Life.seasons_to_days). Only MATURE trees can be felled: it takes `chops` axe blows, the cut marks showing the damage; a hurt tree heals after heal_minutes. Felling a mature tree gives sapling_count sapling(s) with chance sapling_chance (the player only); the player plants one on free grass in front of them. Development only: the command-line flag --tree-growth N (honoured only in debug builds, see docs/TREES.md) makes trees grow N times faster.

fruit_trees._note: B14 (asset pipeline: Craftpix fruit trees): a grown fruit tree bears `item` (yield a picking) in the fruiting seasons; picked bare, it bears again regrow_seasons later (calendar seasons, rounded to whole days), at dawn, but only in a fruiting season. Village trees within orchard_house_range tiles of a house door become orchard trees one in orchard_share by a hash of their cell (new worlds; saved worlds keep their trees). Felled, they give logs and (by tree_growth.sapling_chance) a sapling like any tree. Agent proposal, provisional.

_plants_note: Wild flowers and berry bushes (owner B8-015/B8-016): a picked plant is bare, and ripe again at the dawn this many calendar seasons later (plant_regrow_seasons, rounded to whole days by Life.seasons_to_days; TIME-02). field_grow_seasons: a sown village field ripens this many seasons later. Agent proposal, provisional: balance review pending (docs/BUILD_DECISIONS.md).
_caravan_note: TEMPORARY PLACEHOLDER (owner 2026-10-20, CARAVAN-TMP): caravan_allowance (30 coins a day) is an adjustable stand-in for outside settlements that are not yet simulated, not a permanent rule; Expansion B (EXP-B, SET-C) replaces it with trade from real demand and purchasing power. The caravan is a finite regional market (B7-014): it holds a purse that starts at caravan_float, gains up to caravan_allowance coins a day (the region's demand for the village's surplus; less as the village's coins approach caravan_ceiling_per_head a head, and nothing at the ceiling; never above caravan_float) and every coin the village pays it for ore, coal and stone, and spends at most caravan_coins a visit and never more than it holds. The village's currency can only grow by the allowance and never past the ceiling. Agent proposal, provisional - balance review pending.
_property_note: Property and land (owner rules 2026-10-18: the manor sells and lets land and houses, rent weekly; the numbers are agent proposals, provisional: balance review pending, docs/BUILD_DECISIONS.md 'Property and land'). plot_price is a 9x10 plot's price, other ground by area; house_price a house with its ground; a week's rent is weekly_rent_share of the price; the manor buys back at sell_back_share; rent_evict_missed unpaid weeks end a lease; a vacant stall is let rent-free to a villager out of work with stall_min_coins to stock it.
_stall_note: Player market stall (PL1-10 stages 1-2, agent proposals, provisional): rent per game day paid to the manor; mornings of unpaid rent before the manor takes the pitch back; how near (tiles) the player must be for sales; how far (tiles) a villager will walk to buy; buyers sent per game hour; most pieces one visit buys; most kinds of goods listed; sales kept in the record; a buyer pays up to this much more per urgency level over the dearest local price; coins a non-trader keeps back.
_shop_note: PL1-10 stages 3-4 (agent proposals, provisional: balance review pending, docs/BUILD_DECISIONS.md 'Player businesses, stages 3 and 4'). A larger stall costs stall_large_cost once (to the manor) and then stall_large_rent_day a day, holds stall_large_listings kinds, may show one item on a display that draws buyers stall_large_reach times as far. A shop: shop_licence_day a day to the manor, shop_listings kinds on the counter and shop_shelf_listings more for each shelves (at most shop_max_shelves), each stock chest (at most shop_max_chests) holds shop_store_per_chest spare pieces and refills a sold-out kind with shop_restock. shop_equipment: the materials each piece of equipment takes from the pack. An attendant is paid attendant_wage coins every morning from the till, then the purse.
_construction_note: Property phase 2 (owner rules 2026-10-18: free placement anywhere legal, ground bought or leased on the spot; materials only; helpers hired for coin carry the owner's goods; crowded households split; workshops are buildings with stations, built after a house). Every number here is an agent proposal, provisional: balance review pending (docs/BUILD_DECISIONS.md 'Property and construction, phase 2'). workshop_cost: materials per workshop kind; workshop_price: a workshop with its ground, as house_price is a house's; helper_wage: a day's carrying, paid by the employer when hired (the manor's day wage); split_*: a household whose living members outnumber its house's beds founds a new household when, after paying for the new home, it keeps split_keep_base + split_keep_per_member coins a member staying behind; founder_build_days: the helper days a founder budgets for.
_module_note: PL2-008/014 (agent proposals, provisional: balance review pending, docs/BUILD_DECISIONS.md 'Modular property'). module_price: what a room added to a property is worth with its ground, as workshop_price is a workshop's (kinds not listed use workshop_price); a week's rent and the manor's buy-back follow from it as for any building. workshop_cost holds every module kind's materials. The small room (HOUSE-10, owner OD-14, 2026-10-20: a 5x6 bedroom-sized addition with two beds) costs about half the quarters for a third of the ground; its materials and price are agent proposals, provisional like the rest.

loft._note: HOUSE-12 (owner-approved 2026-10-20, docs/directives/2026-10-20_loft_and_actions_approval.md): a sleeping loft under a house's roof, built like any building (materials delivered, the beds only when finished); cost its materials, beds its sleeping places (bed sharing applies), per_house the most a house can have.

bed_share._note: HOUSE-08 (owner, OD-13, 2026-10-20: young children may share beds within reasonable age limits; couples may share beds). Partners living together share one bed; children below life.child_until share children_per_bed to a bed; adolescents, adults and elders need a bed each. children_per_bed is an agent proposal, provisional until the balance review.

_found_note: EQ-07 (agent proposal, provisional): a founding household starts its house with the ground and found_start_share of the materials' price in hand and buys the rest as it earns, instead of needing the whole price first; couples who live apart, or a grown child and partner in a full house, found households (Construction.couples_needing_home). founder_build_days is no longer used for the start.
_apothecary_note: PL1-04 (agent proposal, provisional): the sage keeps the village apothecary. Starting stock, flowers the sage buys (BUYS sage) and brews into poultices and tonics at the stove, and the caravan's finite resupply: on each visit it sells the sage up to caravan_apothecary_per_visit pieces towards caravan_apothecary_stock, at the item's base value, paid from the sage's own coins above the trader cash floor (coins leave the village, like the ore imports).

animals._note: Owner rules: animals get hungry and die unfed like the villagers; keepers and the player feed livestock, wild animals graze; a well-fed male and female breed; babies use the baby sheets (half scale of the adult sheet where there is none) until grown; juvenile_years/grow_years/elder_years/death_years are the stages in calendar years (TIME-02: read through Life.years_to_days), death_years the range of natural death for the elderly; animals become meat. The numbers are agent proposals (docs/BUILD_DECISIONS.md). start = [males, females] per pen or per wood; keep = breeding adults that hunters and keepers leave; feed = wheat per meal.

_reserve_note: OD-19 (owner 2026-10-20, docs/directives/2026-10-20_od19_dynamic_reserves.md): no fixed coin reserve. Each person's reserve is World.necessity: what their household foreseeably needs over reserve_days days, from what it can know (its members' food need less the food it holds, a log a night less the logs it holds, a medicine for each member hurt below home_production.medicine_use_below who has none, rent falling due), less the wages its paid members can expect after the first day while the treasury can pay them, priced at what the market asks now, less the coins the rest of the household holds. Food, fuel and medicine may be bought with reserved coins; stock, materials and other buys keep it. reserve_days is the agent's planning horizon, an agent proposal.

wildlife._note: B14 (owner: forest animals roam and feed on their own; carnivores hunt and eat the grazers, grazers graze; owner answers 2026-10-19). Hunters (diet hunt, and the bear as an omnivore) that are hungry kill one of their prey species in their wood, at most hunt_chance_per_hour an hour, never taking a species below its keep; near the player the chase is seen (chase_speed x speed, the kill within kill_range). Prey flee a hunter within its flee distance. The bear eats a ripe berry bush within berry_range of its wood first. A hungry fox takes a pen chicken at night (night_from to night_to) at fox_raid_chance_per_hour, never below the pen's keep. Wolves and bears ('people': true) fight back for anger_seconds when struck, and one below people_hunger hunger goes for a person standing in its wood with nobody else within alone_radius tiles; foxes never attack people. Nobody takes the last grown male or female of a kind in a wood, and the village hunter leaves hunter_spare more than a kind's keep for the predators. A hunter breeds only while its wood holds prey_per_predator spare prey for each of its kind and one more, and a wood's last pair of a hunting kind (at its keep) scavenges (hunger back to scavenge_hunger) rather than starve (these floors do not stop old age, so alone they let every kind die out: the breeding refuges, balance 'refuges', WR-01, keep a kind from global extinction). Foxes, like the bear, eat ripe berries by their wood first. Agent proposal, provisional.

refuges._note: WR-01 (owner directive 2026-10-19, Part II; World Design Rule 018): protected breeding refuges, one per wood and wild species (respecting a species' 'only' woods). A refuge's breeding stock is a hidden count, never an animal: nothing sees, strikes, hunts, loots or eats it and no update lowers it. At dawn, once interval_years (calendar years) have passed since its last cohort and in one of its seasons, it produces one litter (the species' litter x stock/2), but only up to the room its woods have below release_below of the species' woods_cap (never less than a pair) (young already travelling count) and only where they can feed (grazers: the wood's grass not overgrazed; hunters and omnivores: wildlife.prey_per_predator spare prey for each of their kind and one more); otherwise it waits without resetting. The young stay inside until juvenile_years old, then leave at dawn as juveniles; any with no room by grow_years stay hidden for good. Each young goes to the wood with the lowest share of its cap (another wood counts cross_wood_penalty more), entering from the refuge or, for another wood, after travelling unseen (lost on the way at transit_loss); there it walks at disperse_speed of its speed to a settling point disperse [min, max] tiles away, the farthest of `samples` cells from others of its kind and its littermates (up to 3 x spacing), and settles there or after settle_days. Near the player a dispersing animal wanders aside wander_share of its steps. place 'deep' puts the refuge on the fifth of the wood's cells farthest from the village. Agent proposal, provisional.

_od16_note: OD-16 (owner 2026-10-20: (b) the manor supports the essential trades from its treasury, (a) bandit coins recirculate, (c) the caravan buys more surplus). Every number here is an agent proposal, provisional until the balance review. manor_support_floor_days: the days of obligations the treasury keeps when buying workers' tools or paying a smith in advance (EQ-19); manor_orders_per_smith: advances open per smith; manor_order_days: days an advance order stays open before it lapses. bandit_spend_min: coins a bandit holds before slipping into the market to buy food; bandit_spend_units: food bought a trip (EQ-20). loot_recover_hours: hours loot with coins lies before guards collect it for the treasury; guard_loot_range: tiles from a guard on duty (EQ-20). caravan_producer_keep: what a producer keeps of each good the caravan buys directly from producers (EQ-21).
_government_note: Manor treasury, taxes, wages, granary and relief (owner-approved B3 plan, docs/BUILD_DECISIONS.md). Days are measured in the treasury's daily obligations (wages).
_manor_job_note: A manor job's wage is set aside while the treasury keeps this many days of obligations after it (B7-009): the line the evening's repairs already use (3 days of wages). treasury_reserve_days (10) stays for tax rates and for hiring staff. Agent proposal, provisional - balance review pending.
_household_note: Household economics and job mobility (docs/BUILD_DECISIONS.md): agent proposals using existing jobs and wages.
_succession_note: Essential trades are handed on (B8-016, owner 2026-10-19: apprentice, then newcomer; the numbers are agent proposals, provisional): when a smith, carpenter, tanner, cook, tavernkeeper or merchant dies, and when the last farmer, woodcutter or miner does, the post is open for succession_days; then an adult without a trade (the dead worker's household first) takes it as an apprentice; with none, a newcomer arrives with the next caravan (at the latest newcomer_max_days after the death) with newcomer_coins of their own and takes the post, the workstation and a home.
_theft_note: Theft, shops and containers (owner rules 2026-10-18; the numbers are agent proposals, docs/BUILD_DECISIONS.md). A guard who sees a theft, or questions a seller of stolen goods, returns the goods and fines theft_fine coins to the treasury; a caught pickpocket is reported by its victim and witnesses (PICK-01, owner OD-20 2026-10-21; the report rules), not heard. guard_call_radius: how near a guard must be to an owner offered their own goods.

skill_start._note: PAR-01A (owner's final directive, 2026-10-20, section 2): only at initial world generation (and once, when an older save without skills is loaded), each established villager is given the experience of a plausible history in their trade: a tenure of between tenure_min and 1.0 of their working years since from_age (a fixed share per person: their id and the world seed), at most max_tenure_years, at xp_per_year, in the skills job_skills names for that trade only. Not age alone, not maximum proficiency: by the player's curve 300 a year makes a two-year apprentice level 3 or below and a 25-year master level 8. Newcomers, children coming of age, career changes and the player get none. Numbers are agent proposals.

report._note: PAR-05 (owner's final directive, section 9: a witness or the victim reporting an attack): a villager who saw an attack, or was its victim, tells a guard: at once if one is in sight (witness_radius), else they walk to the nearest awake guard within range tiles; the report lapses after hours. Agent proposals.

rest._note: PAR-03 (owner OD-18.3, 2026-10-20: the player's recovery model for everyone): a rest that lasts until the morning (WAKE), or day_minutes by day, without being woken, restores health to its cap (World.rest_recover). A villager below seek_below of their health with no medicine to hand rests by day. day_minutes is the player's existing 2-hour rest; seek_below is an agent proposal.

home_production._note: B14 (owner: villagers make food and medicine at home for their own use): a villager below medicine_use_below of their health uses a medicine they carry or the household keeps, else buys one from the Apothecary; in the evening adults forage ripe village plants within forage_range of home (flowers until the household can brew, berries up to berries_keep) and brew poultices at the home hearth up to poultice_keep. Agent proposal, provisional.

carts._note: B14 (owner: carts from logs, planks, ore, coal and iron, a smithy and a carpenter; villagers build from scratch or buy components and assemble). The carpenter saws wheels while it holds wheel_min_planks planks, up to wheel_stock, and assembles handcart_stock handcarts for sale, buying the axle and ironwork from the smith; the smith forges one axle and one ironwork at a time. A storefront household adult with cart_coins of their own buys the parts they lack and assembles a handcart at a workbench, or buys a finished one from the carpenter when that is cheaper. Agent proposal, provisional.
carts._note_use: B14 carts in play (owner answers 2026-10-19): a set-down handcart holds stacks kinds of goods; pulling one walks at pull_speed of the normal speed, the cart trailing trail tiles behind. Only the owner, their family or their hired help may pull or fill one; taking from another's cart is theft. stops are cart stops by the market: the player's cart parked at one within deliver_range of the player's stall is unloaded into the stall store by its attendant each hour. A household with a cart and trip_min surplus goods in store takes them to the market merchants in it (load_minutes to load). Agent proposal, provisional.

_storefront_note: B14: a storefront is a counter built against a held house's front wall beside the door, from storefront_cost taken from the pack; it opens as a shop (shop_listings kinds) with no rent or licence, as it stands on the household's own ground. Agent proposal, provisional.
_station_wait_note: Build 13: a villager arriving at a station the player is working at waits beside it this many game minutes, then gives the place up (its reservation released) and plans again. Agent proposal, provisional.
_cheese_note: Build 13: a villager buying a meal with at least tavern_spare_coins buys cheese (when the vendor has it) with this chance; otherwise the meal with the most food per coin at today's price (NPCBrain._meal_choice). Agent proposal, provisional.
_theft_fine_note: Build 13 economy rule 4: a theft is counted by what was taken. Each crime record carries the items, the quantity and their base value (World.witness); a guard's fine is theft_fine plus theft_fine_share of the value of the goods in question (World.theft_fine_for), so emptying a chest costs more than taking one loaf. Agent proposal, provisional.
_lockpick_note: Chests, locks and lockpicking (PL2-002, agent proposals, docs/BUILD_DECISIONS.md). Chance = lockpick_base + lockpick_per_skill per Stealth level above 1 - lockpick_per_lock per lock level above 1, kept between lockpick_min and lockpick_max. A failed attempt snaps the pick with lockpick_break. An attempt takes lockpick_minutes game minutes per lock level. A success is only seen within lockpick_quiet x the witness radius; a failure or a snapped pick is seen at the full radius.

player_combat._note: B14 combat-quality issue CQ-01 (owner: sword presses lost, hits needing sprite overlap). A swing: windup seconds from the press to the blow (the sword sheet draws its slash on the third frame, 0.16 s in), then recovery for the rest of the swing time (0.6 s times the Combat tier attack_time). A press while swinging is kept when buffer seconds or less remain, and one press at most. The blow lands on the nearest body within reach tiles whose direction is within the arc ahead (cosine arc_cos, about 70 degrees each side) or within close tiles in any direction, with a clear line (no wall or solid cell between); foes first. The touch Attack button swings at a foe within reach; tap-to-strike walks only into reach. Agent proposal, provisional.

farming._note: PL2-015 farming by the player (docs/BUILD_DECISIONS.md 'Farming'; every number is an agent proposal, provisional). Land: only ground the player owns or leases. Tilling a cell: by hand (no tool, slow and tiring) or with the hand plough (the baseline); a draught animal is deferred. seconds are real seconds; stamina is taken at the start and the player needs that much to begin (stamina regenerates player_stamina_regen_per_second). Crops grow by an hourly progress step: 1 / (days * 24) times the season's rate, ripe at 1; no sowing in sow_seasons-excluded seasons (winter), growth slows in autumn and stops in winter. yield is the crop item per cell, seeds_back the seed items a harvest returns (seed saving), seed_price what a farmer or the food merchant charges for a seed. pens: [width, height] of a player pen by species; fence cells cost one plank per fence_cells_per_plank. animal_price is an adult's price from the keeper (young_price_share for a juvenile). products: what an adult pen animal gives (sex f/any) every `days` game days while well fed, kept in the pen (product_cap each) until collected.
farming._seed_note: Build 13 economy rule 3: seed is stock, never made from nothing. Sellers (farmers, the food merchant) start with seed_stock; a farmer saves seed_keep wheat seed from each field harvest (taken from the crop) up to seed_cap; each caravan visit sells the food merchant up to caravan_seed_per_visit seeds towards caravan_seed_stock, at seed value from the merchant's own coins above the trader cash floor (coins leave the village). The player saves seed from their own harvests (seeds_back). Agent proposal, provisional.
